title: Newcastle’s Jaissle wants to scream as Grealish leaves Moyes speechless
content: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! While it is customary for fans of top-flight clubs with delusions of grandeur to cope with Fizzy Cup exits by pretending the competition is beneath them, this is no longer an option that is open to supporters of Newcastle United. Winning the trophy sponsored by a low-calorie, fruit-flavoured energy drink brand from Thailand may only rank fifth in the domestic pecking order behind the Premier League, FA Cup and both transfer windows, but nobody will ever forget how much it meant to hundreds of thousands of overjoyed Geordies when their team did exactly that the season before last to end a trophy drought dating back to the Jurassic era. And with a quarter-final trip to the tough-tackling League Two bullyboys of Fleetwood up for grabs during their match against serial trophy-dodgers Everton last night, the travelling Toon Army must have fancied their chances of being in the shake-up again. I clearly remember the first time I laughed out hard and loud, as a 12-year-old, reading Three Men in a Boat by Jerome K Jerome. Tonight, 50 years later, after a stretch of horrendous bad years and months (and for my mental health, I exclude the struggles of Tottenham), I read the Football Daily column. Its is often quite witty, but this time, reading about some penalty kick gone awry … I know, I have a simplistic sense of humour, but I laughed so hard and cried at the same time, that my family wondered what happened. Thanks for a cathartic experience. Words” – L Json. As a Spurs supporter who saw my first game at White Hart Lane when I was five years old – almost eight decades ago – I can only express my relief that attention has drifted away from the continual ridicule of my team. The fact that a certain club that should return to south of the Thames managed to lose at Highbury (ironically), that lot from down Kings Road and Manchester United are all hogging the headlines for all the wrong reasons just makes life sweeter. It’s time for my second nap of the day now, so I’ll sign off” – Stewart McGuinness. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. summary: Newcastle’s Jaissle expressed a desire to scream during a recent event. Grealish’s performance left manager Moyes speechless.

title: Alex de Minaur defeats Alexander Zverev to reach Vienna Open final
content:
Alex de Minaur, the world No 10, defeated the world No 1‑elect Alexander Zverev 6‑4, 1‑6, 7‑6 (7‑4) in the Vienna Open semi‑final.  The Australian’s attacking style and a decisive tiebreaker—where he brushed off a couple of double faults—kept pressure on the two‑time Grand Slam champion.

The victory propels de Minaur into the championship match against Carlos Alcaraz at the Wiener Stadthalle, a win he has called one of the most significant of his career.
summary: Alex de Minaur defeated world No 1-elect Alexander Zverev 6-4, 1-6, 7-6 (7-4) in the Vienna Open semi‑final. The win sets up a final against Carlos Alcaraz at the Wiener Stadthalle.

title: Atlanta Dream take early lead in Game 7 against Golden State Valkyries
content:
The 2026 WNBA Finals Game 7 is a winner‑take‑all matchup between the Atlanta Dream and the Golden State Valkyries, with both teams vying for their first championship. The Valkyries are hosting the Dream at their home venue.

In the first quarter, Atlanta built an 11‑2 run to take its first lead of the game. Rhyne Howard’s turnaround fadeaway gave the Dream a 11‑10 advantage with 2 minutes and 16 seconds remaining in the opening quarter.
summary: The Atlanta Dream lead 11-10 over the Golden State Valkyries after an 11‑2 run in the first quarter. Rhyne Howard scored a turnaround fadeaway to give the Dream their first lead with 2 minutes and 16 seconds remaining in the opening quarter.

title: Canelo Álvarez Reclaims WBC Title in Riyadh Amid Houthi Attack Concerns
content:
Saúl “Canelo” Álvarez reclaimed the WBC super‑middleweight title with a unanimous‑decision victory over the previously unbeaten Christian Mbilli in Riyadh on Saturday night. The bout was held at Kingdom Arena, with Álvarez winning by unanimous decision.

The fight proceeded amid a week of heightened security concerns in the Saudi capital. Saudi‑led coalition officials said they had intercepted missiles and drones launched by Iran‑aligned Houthi forces.

Several events in the kingdom were cancelled or postponed because of the security situation, including the Six Kings Slam tennis exhibition.
summary: Saúl “Canelo” Álvarez won a unanimous decision over Christian Mbilli to regain the WBC super‑middleweight title in Riyadh. The fight proceeded at Kingdom Arena despite heightened security after the Saudi‑led coalition intercepted missiles and drones launched by Iran‑aligned Houthi forces, causing cancellations of events such as the Six Kings Slam tennis exhibition.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Maresca blames “silly” errors after City lose to Brighton 1-0
content: Matheus Nunes mistake lets in Yasin Ayari for winner Maresca: ‘We are conceding silly goals that we can avoid’ Enzo Maresca said “silly goals” and individual errors are costing Manchester City after Matheus Nunes’ mistake allowed Yasin Ayari to score Brighton’s winner in Saturday’s 1-0 victory here. Ayari’s strike was made possible after Nunes, City’s right-back, missed Diego Gómez’s cross from the right, so the ball could come back across goal via Maxim De Cuyper. The 2-1 loss at Aston Villa came from Gianluigi Donnarumma allowing Nicolas Jackson’s long-range winner to squeeze under his body.
summary: Enzo Maresca said Manchester City are conceding “silly goals” after Matheus Nunes’ mistake allowed Yasin Ayari to score Brighton’s winner in a 1-0 defeat. He also cited a 2-1 loss at Aston Villa where Gianluigi Donnarumma let Nicolas Jackson score a long‑range winner.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Lewis Hamilton takes first Ferrari pole at Mexican Grand Prix, Antonelli fourth
content: George Russell second on grid after qualifying Antonelli well placed as he nears title confirmation Even as Formula One’s young gun Kimi Antonelli remains on course to claim his first world championship on Sunday it was the veteran, seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton who gave a salutary reminder that there is very much fight left in the old dog yet as he claimed a spectacular pole position for the Mexico City Grand Prix. Hamilton delivered a superb lap for Ferrari to secure his first pole for the team and just beat Mercedes’ George Russell into second. World champion in waiting Antonelli was in fourth place but remains in position to close out the title on Sunday, although Hamilton and Russell, who must win the race to have any hope of keeping the fight alive, have at least locked out the front row.
summary: Lewis Hamilton secured his first pole position for Ferrari at the Mexico City Grand Prix, edging out Mercedes driver George Russell who qualified second. Kimi Antonelli qualified fourth, keeping him in contention for the title.

content: Esteban Ocon has refuted reports suggesting his removal by Haas at the Mexico City Grand Prix resulted from a dispute with team principal Ayao Komatsu that escalated into a physical confrontation. Ocon says no such altercation occurred.
summary: Esteban Ocon denied reports that his being dropped by Haas at the Mexico City Grand Prix was due to a row with team principal Ayao Komatsu. He said no physical confrontation took place.

content: Nottingham Forest head coach Oliver Glasner warned that, without an improvement in results, he could become the club’s fifth sacking in just over a year. He said the pressure to secure wins is increasing and that his position depends on a swift turnaround.
summary: Oliver Glasner is the head coach of Nottingham Forest. He said he may become the club’s fifth sacking in just over a year unless results improve soon.

content: Manchester United have accumulated nine points after seven league matches. At that rate, projecting the same pace over a full season would yield fewer than 30 points, a total that would typically place a club in relegation danger.

title: North Korean hacking group linked to $6.3B Binance breach
content: A North Korea‑based cybercrime group is identified as the source of a $6.3 billion hack of the cryptocurrency exchange Binance. Blockchain intelligence firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis linked the incident—the largest crypto hack on record—to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking unit previously known for targeting the digital‑asset sector.
summary: A North Korea-based cybercrime group is alleged to have hacked Binance for $6.3 billion. Blockchain intelligence firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis tied the breach to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking unit that has previously targeted the digital asset industry.

title: ‘You Can See Everything’ film critiques modern manufactured reality
content: The film “You Can See Everything,” created by Fielder and Oppenheim, presents a view in which everything can be seen, yet the creators emphasize that seeing does not equal knowing. According to the description, the film’s effectiveness stems from its awareness of this distinction.
summary: The film “You Can See Everything” shows that seeing everything does not equal knowing. Directors Fielder and Oppenheim make the film effective by recognizing this distinction.

title: Blackburn's governor bid opens possible Senate seat for Defense Secretary Hegseth
content: Sen. Marsha Blackburn (R‑Tenn.) is running for Tennessee’s governorship, creating a vacancy in the state’s Senate delegation. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, a former Army National Guard major, has expressed interest in the open Senate seat and is regarded as a likely oversight target in the next Congress should House Democrats win the majority.
summary: Sen. Marsha Blackburn’s (R-Tenn.) bid to become Tennessee’s next governor is leaving a potential opening for Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, who is viewed as one of the top oversight targets in the next Congress if House Democrats take the majority.
author: The Hill

title: New autism study complicates Trump administration’s search for cause
content: A newly published study identified links between specific maternal health conditions during pregnancy and autism diagnoses across racial and ethnic groups. The research, conducted by investigators at the New York University Grossman School of Medicine and the Kaiser Permanent School of Medicine, highlights the limited understanding that persists as the Trump administration seeks a cause of autism.
summary: New autism study complicates Trump administration’s search for cause.

title: El‑Sayed accuses Stevens of relitigating primary after she urges apology on Israel
content:
Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El‑Sayed (D) rebuked former primary rival Rep. Haley Stevens (D‑Mich.) after she said he should apologize for comments he made about Israel, a demand made only days before the upcoming Senate contest.  

Stevens responded that she would appear alongside El‑Sayed for the first time since their August primary.
summary: Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed (D) is firing back on his former primary opponent, Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Mich.), after she expected him to apologize over his comments on Israel just a few days out from the high-stakes Michigan Senate race.

content: Mississippi Democratic Senate candidate Scott Colom released a “Sinners”-themed campaign advertisement on TikTok over Halloween weekend, just days before the midterm elections. The spot references an Academy Award‑winning film set in the 1932 Mississippi Delta starring Michael B. Jordan as twins, using the movie’s premise as a backdrop for the ad.
summary: Mississippi Democratic Senate candidate Scott Colom released a “Sinners”-themed campaign ad over Halloween weekend, days before the midterm elections. The TikTok ad references the Academy Award‑winning film set in the Mississippi Delta in 1932 starring Michael B. Jordan as twins.

content:

title: Jonathan Wilson: Mikel Arteta's "dossier" strategy is dangerous for Arsenal
content: The manager is not yet in Alex Ferguson and José Mourinho’s league, but his conspiracy theories have reached new levels English football loves the word “dossier”. It doesn’t love dossiers themselves, of course; they’re for nerds – unless, that is, they’re a “secret dossier”, which have a thrilling redolence of spy dramas, invisible ink and dead drops. Non-secret dossiers, though, are inherently risible: call something a “dossier” in English football and you’re immediately signalling: this is absurd poindextering. Dossiers were preposterous when Don Revie was – imagine the pretension! – drawing up scouting reports on opposing players, and they are preposterous today as Mikel Arteta collates images of rival managers stepping outside their technical area. Arteta, it should be said, did not use the word “dossier”; rather it was swiftly applied to what he had called “a massive storage of images”. During Arsenal’s 2-0 win against Everton last Saturday, he received his second booking of the season for leaving his technical area. This, it turns out, is another part of the vast conspiracy against Arsenal. Yes, Arteta accepted, he left his technical area (44 times before being booked, according to the former referee Graham Scott), but other managers do it too. “There are managers who have the record in the league, 36 times in 10 minutes [they] leave the touchline – no yellows,” he said. “I am clipping all of that … so if somebody comes to me I can say: ‘I am not in the record yet.’ Somebody else has the record so let’s see. Then it’s 36 yellow cards in 10 minutes for the managers.”
summary: Mikel Arteta collected images of rival managers leaving their technical areas after receiving his second booking for doing so. Jonathan Wilson argues that this approach, which Arteta defends as a counter to perceived bias, is a dangerous tactic for the club.

Despite the setback, Northampton weathered the loss to score 28 unanswered points after withstanding Gloucester’s early onslaught.

The performance marked a stark contrast to Northampton’s previous league outing, where 119 points were scored. This victory was built on strong defensive efforts, with Tom Pearson, who is back in the England picture this autumn, delivering an outstanding display throughout the game.

content:

While acknowledging the severity of conceding in that manner, Carrick stated he is now concentrating on preparing his players for the midweek fixture.

title: Nighttime bat surveys aid science and reshape public perception
content:
People often react with curiosity when they hear a chirping sound on a detector or feel something whiz past, moments that signal an encounter with microbats. The title notes that seeking these animals after dark can aid scientific research and shift public perception of the creatures.

Microbats are described as small, primarily nocturnal mammals that navigate and hunt using ultrasonic echolocation. They emit calls and listen to the returning echoes to locate objects and prey.
summary: Researchers conduct after‑dark searches for microbats, which are small nocturnal mammals that navigate and hunt using ultrasonic echolocation. The resulting data can advance scientific knowledge and change how people view these animals.

title: NES Contra 1987 ported from assembly to C and WebAssembly with online co‑op
content:
A Show HN post announces a browser‑based port of the 1987 NES game Contra. The author used vermiceli’s annotated disassembly of the original ROM as a reference, translating the 6502 assembly routine by routine into C and verifying each frame against the original using the Mesen emulator. The resulting C code was then compiled to WebAssembly, allowing the game to run in a web browser.

The port adds online multiplayer, enabling two players to cooperate over the internet. The project’s source code is hosted on GitHub, and the submission has received 28 points and 17 comments on Hacker News.
summary: The 1987 NES game Contra was translated routine‑by‑routine from its 6502 assembly into C and then compiled to WebAssembly to run in a browser. The port adds online multiplayer so two players can play co‑op over the internet.

title: Pakistan clinch tri-series final as Fakhar Zaman scores 127 to beat Sri Lanka
content:
Pakistan clinched the tri‑series title in a dramatic final at Lahore’s Gaddafi Stadium. The packed-out venue saw the match settled in the penultimate over, with Pakistan defeating Sri Lanka by three wickets to win the tournament under the lights.

In the chase of 326, Fakhar Zaman delivered the headline performance, smashing 127 off 99 balls. After his dismissal the new batsmen had to remain composed, and the partnership that followed proved decisive.

Arafat Minhas (21) and Hasan Nawaz (24) forged a 94‑run stand that secured the win. Minhas and Faheem Ashraf were dismissed with two runs still required, but Shaheen Afridi finished the evening with a powerful boundary over the ropes. Sri Lankan opener Kamindu Mendis also scored 131, but his efforts could not prevent Pakistan’s victory.
summary: Pakistan beat Sri Lanka by three wickets in the tri-series final at Gaddafi Stadium, Lahore, chasing 326. Fakhar Zaman made 127 off 99 balls, supported by a 94‑run partnership from Arafat Minhas and Hasan Nawaz, and Shaheen Afridi hit the winning runs.

title: Boot Sector Language Model Generates Infinite Linux Boot Logs
content:
A new language model project has been showcased on Hacker News, featuring an inference engine that fits entirely within a 510-byte Master Boot Record (MBR). The project draws inspiration from the boot sector demo scene, where developers previously created applications such as chess games and C compilers in 512 bytes. This neural network generates Linux boot logs for non-existent hardware by producing dmesg messages infinitely. The system utilizes a small character-level network trained on dmesg data, with the weights, vocabulary, and strings stored in the sectors immediately following the MBR.

During development, the creator identified a specific bug by comparing the output of a Python simulator with the assembly code running in QEMU. Although the initial characters matched, the output eventually diverged. By retrieving hidden layer values via QEMU’s debug port, it was determined that only the first neuron was calculated correctly. The issue stemmed from the idiv instruction, which stores its remainder in the edx register, overwriting the pointer to the biases table. This caused the first neuron to be biased correctly while subsequent neurons used garbage data. The fix involved determining the bias address from the loop counter to ensure no pointers survived the division operation.

A second bug was discovered by inspecting the code before the initial run. The BIOS print routine zeros out the bx register, which contained the predicted character number. This necessitated the use of push and pop instructions to preserve the value of bx around the print call. The project contrasts with Sectorllm, which runs a 5-layer Llama2 model with an attention mechanism in 1.2K of assembly code. In contrast, this project prioritizes fitting the engine into a single sector, resulting in a network with just one hidden layer of int8 operations.
summary: A 510‑byte MBR contains an inference engine that uses a small char‑level neural network to generate Linux boot messages infinitely. The author debugged integer‑arithmetic bugs, fixing bias pointer and BIOS print routine issues to match QEMU output.

title: Government corruption tops concerns of US midterm voters, poll shows
content:
A recent exclusive poll indicates that government corruption has emerged as a top issue for voters heading into the US midterm elections. The article highlights that alleged self-dealing by the president and his allies is becoming a significant concern for the electorate. This shift in voter sentiment contrasts with historical political narratives, such as the “welfare queen” trope popularized by Ronald Reagan in 1976, which focused on fraud by the poor rather than high-level governmental misconduct.

The text details several specific allegations of financial entanglements involving the Trump administration and its associates. It notes that the Qatari government gifted the president a luxury jet, a move that potentially violates the emoluments clause of the constitution. Additionally, the UAE reportedly gained access to high-end American AI chips shortly after an investment firm linked to its ruling family purchased a $500 million stake in World Liberty Financial, a crypto company funded by the families of Trump and Steve Witkoff.

Further examples of alleged self-dealing include the pardons granted to Wanda Vázquez Garced, the former governor of Puerto Rico, and Julio Herrera Velutini, a banker who paid her bribes. These pardons followed a $50 million deal between Velutini’s family and Alina Habba, Trump’s former personal lawyer, as well as a $3.5 million donation to Trump’s Maga Inc Super Pac. The article also points to the Pentagon lending over $600 million to Vulcan Elements, a rare earths startup, three months after Donald Jr’s venture capital firm, 1789 Capital, acquired a stake in the company.

Finally, the piece mentions Powerus, a drone maker backed by Eric and Donald Trump, which is selling drone interceptors to Persian Gulf allies. The source characterizes this as enriching the president’s children from a war launched without consulting Congress. These incidents collectively form the basis for the growing voter concern regarding corruption in the government.
summary: An exclusive poll found that government corruption is a top issue for US midterm voters. The report cites alleged self‑dealing by President Trump and his allies, including a Qatari‑gifted luxury jet, UAE access to American AI chips after a stake purchase, and donations linked to pardons.

With the club preparing to meet the other recent Premier League champions on Sunday, a fourth successive home win could narrow the gap on Arsenal to three points. Seven weeks after a headline‑grabbing Champions League press conference, Mac Allister is among those who feel they deserve a contract extension.
summary: Alexis Mac Allister, the 27‑year‑old Argentine, has shaken off contract doubts and become an indispensable part of Liverpool’s central midfield. Despite a weak negotiating stance, he believes he deserves a contract extension and has helped lift the team’s aggression and intensity under Andoni Iraola.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Manchester United miss chance to close on WSL top three in drab draw at Everton
content:
Manchester United played a quiet draw against Everton at Goodison Park, where a group of school‑age dancers in fancy‑dress costumes celebrated Halloween by performing to Michael Jackson’s “Thriller” during half‑time. The match itself was uneventful, with both sides failing to produce a dramatic finish.

United’s performance was limited by a lack of shots on target. Throughout the first 75 minutes, the team tested Everton goalkeeper Courtney Brosnan only a handful of times, and the visitors’ lack of creativity prevented them from narrowing the gap to the sides in the European qualification spots. The result left United missing an opportunity to close on the WSL top three.
summary: Manchester United missed the opportunity to close on the WSL top three after a drab draw at Everton. The team tested Courtney Brosnan few times and lacked creativity, missing chances to narrow the gap to European qualification spots.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Simon Harmer's six-wicket haul secures South Africa's series win over Australia
content:
South Africa reclaimed the top spot in the ICC Test rankings after winning the three‑Test series in South Africa 2‑1.  Simon Harmer delivered a career‑best performance, taking six wickets for 16 runs at Newlands, and the South African side secured the series victory.

The series was marred by a disastrous morning in Cape Town that saw Australia lose by 176 runs.  On the final day, Australia were dismissed for 111 while chasing 288, a collapse that sealed the 2‑1 defeat.

Australia lost key players Matt Renshaw and Marnus Labuschagne in the opening over at Newlands and were unable to recover.  Pat Cummins’ 90‑ball vigil and Nathan Lyon’s unbeaten 33 helped delay a draw, but the outcome was decided when Harmer dismissed Josh Hazlewood just before tea.
summary: Simon Harmer took a career‑best six for 16 to help South Africa win the three‑Test series 2‑1 over Australia. The defeat also caused Australia to lose the top spot in the Test rankings.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Manchester United crisis deepens after Chelsea defeat
content:
Manchester United’s troubles appear to be worsening after a defeat to Chelsea that saw the club’s striker, Martínez, sent off. The loss has intensified criticism from former players and supporters alike, with old legends expected to voice their discontent and social‑media clips of a fuming Gary Neville circulating widely.

The match also echoed the atmosphere of Erik ten Hag’s final game in charge, as the pressure mounted on Michael Carrick. United squandered several golden opportunities when the score was level, a pattern that had also been seen when Ten Hag was dismissed after a loss to West Ham two years earlier.

Chelsea, meanwhile, capitalised on the situation, turning a poor initial display into a decisive victory. The turnaround has raised concerns about the nascent Xabi Alonso project, as the team’s performance improved dramatically during the match.
summary: Manchester United lost to Chelsea, deepening concerns about the club's future. The match saw United miss golden chances, echoes of Erik ten Hag’s final game, angry supporters and a focus on Michael Carrick, while Chelsea capitalised on a poor initial performance.
author: Guardian Sport

content: Ulster’s quest for an opening win in the United Rugby Championship remains unfulfilled after a 33‑7 loss to the Stormers in Cape Town. The defeat extends Ulster’s search for their first victory of the season.

content:

content: The Trump administration is moving forward with plans to deport Afghan refugees to Afghanistan, despite concerns that they could become targets of the Taliban. title: Cop17 Ends Amid Calls for UN Biodiversity Summit Reforms
content:
Critics have called for significant reforms to United Nations biodiversity summits, arguing that the current system permits a single individual to obstruct progress. This criticism emerged as Cop17, a two-week negotiation session held in Yerevan, Armenia, concluded on Saturday morning. The summit focused on protecting nature and restoring ecosystems, but observers noted that participating nations are likely on track to continue a record of failing to meet targets established over the 34-year history of the convention.

During the closing of the event, governments vowed to intensify their efforts to achieve this decade’s specific goals. These commitments include protecting 30% of the planet for nature, restoring nearly a third of Earth’s degraded ecosystems, and reforming $500 billion in environmentally damaging subsidies. Despite these pledges, the summit ended with growing calls for structural changes to the UN biodiversity process to ensure future targets are actually met.
summary: Cop17 Ends Amid Calls for UN Biodiversity Summit Reforms.

title: Treatment with norrin helps maintain healthy blood vessels and preserve vision in diabetic rats
content: Millions of people in the U.S. are affected by diabetic retinopathy, a diabetes complication that damages the blood vessels in the retina. The retina is the light-sensitive tissue located at the back of the eye. In its early stages, the condition may present no symptoms or only mild problems. However, if the underlying diabetes remains poorly managed, the damage can eventually lead to blindness.
summary: Treatment with norrin helps maintain healthy blood vessels and preserve vision in diabetic rats.

title: Congo's Ebola Deaths Exceed 5,000 Amid Spread to Other African Nations
content:
Congo's Ebola deaths top 5,000 as fear of continent‑wide spread mounts.  

The latest government data released on Saturday confirms that the outbreak has surpassed 5,000 deaths. Congo is grappling with the relentless spread of the disease, and cases have been recorded in other African countries.
summary: Congo's Ebola outbreak has caused more than 5,000 deaths, according to the latest government data. The country is dealing with the disease's continued spread, and cases have been reported in other African nations.

title: Neutrophil RAGE drives early cerebrovascular injury after subarachnoid hemorrhage
content: An international research team from Japan and the United States, led by Assistant Professor Hiroshi Ishii and Professor Osamu Hori and joined by Professors Yasuhiko Yamamoto and Mitsutoshi Nakada of Kanazawa University, has identified neutrophil RAGE (receptor for advanced glycation end products) as a key driver of early cerebrovascular injury after subarachnoid hemorrhage.
summary: Neutrophil RAGE drives early cerebrovascular injury after subarachnoid hemorrhage.

title: Twin study finds artistic creativity linked to poorer mental health, not scientific
content: A recent twin study reports that artistic creativity, unlike scientific creativity, is associated with poorer mental health. The finding adds to a long‑standing debate, as earlier research has produced both links between creativity and mental health difficulties and contradictory or inconsistent results.
summary: A twin study found artistic creativity is linked to poorer mental health, whereas scientific creativity is not. Earlier studies have reported mixed results, with some associating creativity with mental health difficulties and others finding inconsistent findings.

title: Elon Musk Spends $446M on US Midterms, Becoming Largest Single-Cycle Donor
content:
Elon Musk has become the largest single‑cycle political donor in modern U.S. history, according to U.S. Federal Election Commission data collected on 29 October. The tech mogul has contributed at least $445.77 million to Republican‑aligned political action committees and groups during the current election cycle.  

Musk’s contributions have made him the Republican Party’s most prominent financial backer. The scale of his giving has been compared to the cost of half a dozen SpaceX rocket launches or the purchase of thousands of Tesla Cybertrucks. In a more light‑hearted illustration, the amount could also buy more than 31.9 million cheeseburgers at the Tesla Diner in Los Angeles.  

These figures underscore the unprecedented level of private money Musk has poured into the U.S. midterm elections, marking a new milestone in campaign finance history.
summary: Elon Musk Spends $446M on US Midterms, Becoming Largest Single-Cycle Donor.

title: 200 Nations Reach Agreements at U.N. Biodiversity Summit; Missed Opportunities Disappoint
content: Nearly 200 nations reached hard‑fought agreements at the U.N. Biodiversity summit on Friday. The agreements aim to get nature goals back on track, yet many participants expressed disappointment that the outcome missed opportunities to address humanity’s destructive toll on nature.
summary: Nearly 200 nations struck hard-fought agreements Friday at a U. N.

title: Young Canadian Plaintiffs Highlight Mental Health at Climate Change Trial
content:
A landmark Canadian trial has begun, centering on the government’s obligations to combat climate change. Young plaintiffs are suing Ottawa, alleging policy failures.  

During the proceedings, the plaintiffs have directed attention to their mental health, underscoring the psychological impact of climate change on the next generation.
summary: The trial is a landmark Canadian case that examines the government's obligations to fight climate change. Young plaintiffs suing Ottawa over alleged policy failures are seeking to bring attention to their mental health.

title: New oviraptorosaur species Infernogallus jamesi identified as first fruit‑eating dinosaur
content:
Paleontologists from Stony Brook University, the Royal Ontario Museum (ROM), and the North Dakota Geological Survey have identified a new dinosaur species, Infernogallus jamesi. This small oviraptorosaur lived during the Cretaceous period, a time dominated by carnivorous and herbivorous dinosaurs.

Infernogallus jamesi possessed chewing muscles adapted for mashing soft food, indicating it specialized in eating fruit. The discovery marks the first known dinosaur that specifically fed on flowering plants and fruit.
summary: Paleontologists from Stony Brook University, the Royal Ontario Museum and the North Dakota Geological Survey described a new small oviraptorosaur species named Infernogallus jamesi. The species had chewing muscles suited for mashing soft food, making it the first known dinosaur that specifically ate fruit.

title: Rare Iron Age Celtic helmet found crushed in pit at Łysa Góra, Poland
content: Around 2,400 years ago, a group of people at Łysa Góra in Poland took a bronze helmet, crushed it, broke it into pieces, and threw it into a pit with iron adzes and a scythe. Similar helmets are sometimes found in lavish graves of the Celtic warrior elite, from Champagne, France, to Dürrnberg, Austria.
summary: Around 2,400 years ago a bronze helmet was crushed, broken and placed in a pit with iron adzes and a scythe at Łysa Góra in Poland. Similar helmets have been found in lavish Celtic elite graves from Champagne, France, to Dürrnberg, Austria.
author: Phys.org

title: Scientists find bacterial defense that kills itself to stop viruses
content:
Scientists have discovered a bizarre bacterial defense system that works almost completely backward from anything seen before. Unlike typical bacterial immune systems that keep a deadly toxin under control until a virus attacks, this unusual mechanism waits until an infection begins before producing the DNA that switches on its lethal weapon.

The infected bacterium then destroys itself, preventing the virus from multiplying and spreading to neighboring cells.
summary: Scientists discovered a bizarre bacterial defense system that works almost completely backward from anything seen before. The system waits until an infection begins to produce DNA that switches on a lethal weapon, causing the infected bacterium to destroy itself and stop the virus from multiplying and spreading to neighboring cells.

title: 75,000-Year-Old Neanderthal Killed by Wooden Spear Targeting Heart
content: A Neanderthal who died 75,000 years ago may have been killed by a wooden spear aimed at the heart.  The skeleton shows a circular hole in the shoulder blade, indicating the weapon pierced the chest and caused a rapidly fatal injury.  The same individual had previously survived a severe facial injury, suggesting that other Neanderthals may have provided care and support.
summary: A Neanderthal who died 75,000 years ago may have been killed by a wooden spear deliberately aimed at the heart, revealing rare evidence of prehistoric violence. A circular hole in the shoulder blade suggests the weapon pierced the chest and caused a rapidly fatal injury.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists Discover Metals That Resist Cracking at -424°F
content: Scientists have uncovered a mechanism that lets certain metals resist cracking at temperatures as low as –253 °C (–424 °F), where similar materials normally become brittle. In experiments, two alloys reorganize their internal structures, creating new pathways to absorb stress and stay flexible instead of breaking.
summary: Scientists discovered a mechanism that allows certain metals to resist cracking at temperatures as low as -253°C (-424°F). The mechanism involves two experimental alloys reorganizing their internal structures to absorb stress and remain flexible.
author: Science Daily

title: Blood Test May Predict Alzheimer's Risk 10 Years Before Symptoms
content:
A major international study has reported that a simple blood test can predict Alzheimer’s‑related cognitive decline long before symptoms appear. The research indicates that individuals identified as highest risk have a 38 % chance of impairment within five years and an estimated 78 % chance within ten years.  

Scientists say the finding could open the door to earlier intervention and to the development of treatments aimed at preventing Alzheimer’s before memory problems begin.
summary: Blood Test May Predict Alzheimer's Risk 10 Years Before Symptoms.
author: Science Daily

title: Scientists recreate primordial matter by colliding oxygen nuclei
content: Scientists have recreated a primordial state of matter from the universe’s earliest moments by colliding oxygen nuclei at nearly the speed of light. The experiments revealed that the exotic substance can arise in smaller, lower‑energy collisions than previously shown, thereby extending the known limits of early‑universe physics.
summary: Scientists recreated a primordial state of matter from the dawn of the universe by colliding oxygen nuclei at nearly the speed of light. The results show the exotic substance can form in smaller, lower‑energy collisions than previously demonstrated, challenging known boundaries of early‑universe physics.
author: Science Daily

title: 4,000-year-old defensive wall uncovered in Morocco reshapes view of ancient North Africa
content: A 4,000‑year‑old defensive structure uncovered in Morocco is prompting scientists to reassess ancient North African civilizations. The massive fortifications demonstrate a level of prehistoric sophistication that was previously unrecognized and imply that the region contributed more significantly to Mediterranean history than earlier scholarship had acknowledged.
summary: A 4,000-year-old defensive structure has been discovered in Morocco, prompting scientists to revise their understanding of ancient North African civilizations. title: Johns Hopkins scientists identify Bacteroides fragilis toxin as trigger for colon cancer
content: Scientists at Johns Hopkins have identified a missing link between the common gut bacterium Bacteroides fragilis and colorectal cancer. Their research shows that the bacterium’s toxin damages the colon’s protective lining, induces chronic inflammation, and promotes tumor formation, addressing a question that has persisted for nearly two decades.
summary: Scientists at Johns Hopkins uncovered a missing link between the common gut bacterium Bacteroides fragilis and colorectal cancer. The bacterium’s toxin damages the colon’s protective lining, triggers chronic inflammation, and promotes tumor formation.

title: Dame Sue Black discusses the challenges of being an expert witness
content:
Dame Sue Black, recognized as one of the world’s leading forensic anthropologists, has served as an expert witness in a wide range of high‑profile criminal cases.  

Her investigations have taken her from laboratory settings to active war zones and the aftermath of natural disasters, where she has identified victims’ bodies.  

In an interview with Ian Sample, she described standing before a judge and jury as one of the most frightening moments of her career, highlighted the reputational risk of presenting evidence in court, and discussed potential directions for the future of forensic science.
summary: Dame Sue Black, a leading forensic anthropologist, has acted as an expert witness in many high‑profile criminal cases. In an interview with Ian Sample she describes the terror of testifying before a judge and jury, the reputational risk, and her view of forensic science’s future.

title: Construction of DUNE neutrino detectors to begin at former Homestake mine in South Dakota
content:
The town of Lead in South Dakota’s Black Hills grew around a gold rush that drew workers for more than a century. The town’s history is tied to the Homestake mine, once a prolific gold producer.

Today the same mine is being repurposed for a flagship physics experiment. The Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (DUNE) will use the old mine’s deep caverns to search for answers to fundamental questions about the universe.

Construction of DUNE is set to begin on Monday. Engineers will assemble four giant detectors inside caverns blasted from rock a mile underground.
summary: Construction of the Deep Underground Neutrino Experiment (Dune) in the former Homestake mine is due to start on Monday. Engineers will begin assembling four giant detectors inside caverns blasted from rock a mile underground.

content:
Best Buy has announced that it will include a $100 gift card with every preorder of Apple’s new touch‑enabled MacBook Pro. The offer applies to the highest‑end 14‑inch and 16‑inch models, as well as the 14‑inch MacBook Pro equipped with the M6 chip. content:

title: FDA seeks to withdraw approval of experimental vasculitis drug amid study concerns
content:
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration has indicated a desire to withdraw its approval of an experimental medication for a rare autoimmune form of vasculitis, a move the agency says will not be straightforward.  

In a May 2021 briefing document, the FDA outlined its uncertainty about the drug’s value compared with existing treatments and requested input from an independent advisory committee. The study, conducted by California‑based biotech firm ChemoCentryx, showed participants achieving slightly higher rates of symptom remission after one year, but the agency noted that the trial’s design was less than optimal, making the results difficult to interpret. Some advisory members echoed this concern, stating the drug’s effect “is just not well verified by this study.”  

Despite regulatory doubts, many patients and some physicians view the data as promising, hoping the medication could reduce reliance on steroids, which, while effective, often cause severe side effects.
summary: FDA seeks to withdraw approval of experimental vasculitis drug amid study concerns.

title: Seabirds racing home over the ocean can get jet-lagged
content:
A recent study published in Science shows that seabirds can experience jet lag just like humans. The research focused on Manx shearwaters, which fly hundreds of kilometres a day across the North Atlantic. When these birds cross several time zones, their internal rhythms become misaligned, a condition the authors describe as jet lag.

Because Manx shearwaters navigate by the Sun, the misalignment leaves a measurable effect: it skews their compass. The study’s lead author, Patrick Lewin, a behavioural and sensory ecologist at the University of Oxford, noted that the birds’ compass errors provide a clear marker of the jet‑lagged state.

Lewin added that Manx shearwaters are medium‑sized, roughly the same size as a pigeon, white underneath and black on top, with very long wings and a close relation to albatross. The species nest in burrows on coastal islands around the North Atlantic, with most breeding sites in the UK and Ireland and about half of the population residing in Wales.
summary: Flying across several time zones often causes jet lag, a feeling when the body insists it's the middle of the night while the clock says it's lunchtime. Now it turns out this nuisance is not exclusive to humans.
author: Ars Technica

title: 39% of British singles use AI for dating advice, survey finds
content: Almost 40% of British singles have used AI for romantic advice, from writing messages to assessing potential partners After Sam’s ex joked that her sister found him ugly, he turned to AI. Google Gemini had a look at the photo and politely disagreed. AI has been his wingman ever since, aiding his dating life by giving pep talks and vetting his messages. The 27-year-old from Stoke-on-Trent is not the only AI-assisted romantic – a survey of 3,000 British singles published this month by Match Group, the owner of the Tinder and Hinge platforms, found 39% had used AI in their dating lives.
summary: A survey of 3,000 British singles published this month by Match Group found 39% had used AI in their dating lives. The 27-year-old from Stoke-on-Trent, Sam, uses AI, including Google Gemini, to write messages, assess potential partners and give pep talks.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Anthropic files US IPO filing with 92-page AI risk factor document
content:
Anthropic, the developer of the Claude AI model, filed to go public on the US stock market on 26 October. The company’s filing includes a 92-page risk factor document that acknowledges the dangers AI poses to society and humans, as well as factors that could negatively impact its business. Johana Bhuiyan, a senior tech reporter for the Guardian, provides a video explainer breaking down this document.

The analysis highlights that Anthropic’s IPO serves as a significant test for the AI boom. The company is seeking a potentially record-breaking stock market valuation, which represents a key moment for the broader AI industry.
summary: Anthropic, the creator of Claude, filed to go public on the US stock market on 26 October. The company's filing statement contains a 92-page risk factor document in which it acknowledges the dangers that AI poses to society and human beings, and factors that could negatively affect Anthropic's business.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Senegal opens 2026 Youth Olympic Games, first Olympics on African soil
content: The 2026 Youth Olympic Games opened in Dakar, Senegal, with a spectacular ceremony on Saturday, marking the first Olympics held on African soil. The event reflects Africa’s growing role in international sporting competitions.
summary: The 2026 Youth Olympic Games opened with a ceremony on Saturday in Dakar, Senegal. It is the first Olympic event held on African soil as the continent seeks a bigger role in international sporting competitions.
author: France 24

title: Trump moves to curtail voting rights before November 3 midterm elections
content: Americans will cast ballots on November 3 in midterm elections that could result in Republicans losing control of Congress, potentially jeopardizing President Donald Trump’s legislative agenda. Although elections are organized by individual states under the Constitution, Trump has moved to influence the process ahead of the vote.
summary: President Donald Trump is moving to curtail voting rights ahead of the November 3 midterm elections. The elections could see Republicans lose control of Congress, threatening his legislative agenda, even though elections are organized by the states under the Constitution.
author: France 24

title: PSG secure ninth straight win as Achraf Hakimi scores hat‑trick
content:
PSG secured their ninth straight Ligue 1 victory in a dominant performance at the Stade Océane against Le Havre. The French champions thrusted Le Havre into a heavy defeat, with the match described as a “night to remember” for the club.  

Moroccan winger Achraf Hakimi was the match’s standout, scoring a hat‑trick and delivering two assists, contributing to every one of PSG’s five goals. His influence was decisive in the win.  

The result further cemented PSG’s hold on the top of the table, while Le Havre remain at the bottom of the standings.
summary: PSG thrashed Le Havre at the Stade Océane with five goals, all involving Achraf Hakimi’s hat‑trick and two assists. The victory was PSG’s ninth consecutive win, keeping them atop Ligue 1 while Le Havre remain at the bottom.
author: France 24

title: Trump’s MAGA movement shows splits ahead of 2026 midterm elections
content: As the 2026 midterm elections approach, divisions within the MAGA camp are becoming increasingly visible. From the war in Iran and rising fuel prices to the Epstein files, several of Trump’s decisions are fuelling divisions among his most loyal supporters. Once united by a shared vision of America, MAGA now brings together factions that increasingly disagree over foreign policy, the economy and what “America First” should actually mean. Yet Trump remains the central figure holding this political coalition together – and he is fighting to keep it that way. Why are some of the president’s longtime allies distancing themselves from him? Can MAGA remain united despite these disagreements? And can Trump still mobilise his base ahead of the midterms? 🔍 Our journalist Stella Elgersma breaks down the divisions within the MAGA movement and Donald Trump’s strategy to rally his supporters, once again.
summary: Divisions within the MAGA camp are becoming increasingly visible as the 2026 midterm elections approach, fueled by issues such as the war in Iran, rising fuel prices and the Epstein files. Trump remains the central figure trying to hold the coalition together, according to journalist Stella Elgersma.
author: France 24

title: France deploys 70,000 security staff for third weekend of protests
content:
France is preparing for a third weekend of protests, deploying 70,000 security personnel to avoid a repeat of the violence that occurred on October 17. Shops have boarded up their premises, and authorities have warned of further clashes, noting that Halloween raises concerns about masked demonstrators.

The protests began over anger about the cost of living and poor school conditions and have expanded to demand greater civil liberties and the right to protest. With presidential elections six months away, officials have tightened security and restricted demonstrations in several cities.
summary: France is preparing for a third weekend of protests, deploying 70,000 security personnel to avoid a repeat of the October 17 violence. Shops have boarded up, authorities warn of further clashes amid Halloween concerns, and the demonstrations have expanded from cost‑of‑living and school issues to broader civil‑liberty demands as presidential elections approach.
author: France 24

title: Nunez warns of high risk as France readies for third weekend of protests
content:
France’s interior minister, Gérald Nunez, warned that the country faces a high risk of unrest as protests continue. Authorities are preparing for a third consecutive weekend of demonstrations, deploying roughly 70,000 security personnel to avoid a repeat of the violence recorded on October 17.

Shops have boarded up their premises, and officials have highlighted additional security concerns linked to Halloween celebrations and masked demonstrators. The protests, which involve Yellow Vest activists, trade unions and students, began over the rising cost of living, inequality and poor school conditions, and have broadened to demand greater civil liberties and the right to protest.

The actions occur six months before the presidential election, amid a tense political climate and rising support for the far right. Several cities have restricted marches, Paris police have authorised only an outskirts demonstration, and curfews have been imposed in parts of the capital.
summary: France is bracing for a third consecutive weekend of protests, with around 70,000 security personnel deployed to prevent a repeat of the violence seen on October 17. Shops have boarded up their premises as authorities warn of further clashes, with Halloween celebrations adding to security concerns over masked demonstrators.
author: France 24

title: Binance suffers $6.3 billion crypto theft, biggest hack in history
content:
Binance executives are scrambling to recover billions of dollars after the platform was hit by what is being described as the biggest heist in cryptocurrency history. Hackers reportedly stole $6.3 billion from users.

Analysts have pointed the finger at North Korea. The attack exceeds the previous record, which was set in February 2025 when hackers stole $1.5 billion from the crypto exchange Bybit.
summary: Binance executives are scrambling to recover billions of dollars after the crypto platform was hit by what is being described as the biggest heist in cryptocurrency history. Hackers reportedly stole $6.3 billion from users, with analysts pointing the finger at North Korea.
author: France 24

title: Turkey nominates former foreign minister Feridun Hadi Sinirlioglu for UN secretary-general
content: Turkey has nominated Feridun Hadi Sinirlioglu, a former foreign minister and former UN ambassador, for the position of United Nations secretary‑general. The nomination is officially backed by President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, who has publicly called for reform of the UN Security Council.
summary: Turkey nominated its former foreign minister and UN ambassador Feridun Hadi Sinirlioglu for the position of UN secretary-general. The nomination was officially backed by President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, who has called for reform of the UN Security Council.
author: France 24

title: UN political mission in Somalia ends after three decades on Oct. 31
content: The United Nations’ political mission in Somalia will conclude on 31 October, marking the end of three decades of UN political engagement in the Horn of Africa country. Raisedon Zenenga, the UN Secretary‑General’s Deputy Special Representative for Somalia, said the mission’s story has been one of “persistence, partnership and adaptation,” as Somalia looks to the future.
summary: The United Nations political mission in Somalia will conclude on 31 October, ending three decades of engagement. Raisedon Zenenga, the UN Secretary‑General's Deputy Special Representative for Somalia, said the mission was defined by persistence, partnership and adaptation.
author: UN News

title: UN rights official says DPRK's isolation deepens despite new factories and tech
content: A UN rights official says that while the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea is expanding factories and hospitals, introducing smartphones and mobile‑banking services, and enacting new laws at an unprecedented pace, its citizens are now more isolated from the outside world than at any previous point in the country’s history.
summary: DPRK is building factories and hospitals, rolling out smartphones and mobile banking, and passing new laws at an unprecedented rate. Its people are more cut off from the outside world than at any point in the country’s history.
author: UN News

title: Midterm ads accuse Republican candidates of protecting Jeffrey Epstein
content: Ads that allege Republican candidates are “protecting” Jeffrey Epstein have begun airing as the final push toward the midterm elections. Democratic candidates and groups backing them have released the spots, claiming Republicans vote against legislation to release files related to Epstein and thereby shield a pedophile accused of running a sex‑trafficking ring involving minors. The advertisements are described as intended to provoke an emotional response by linking the candidates directly to Epstein’s alleged crimes. Select Democrats are also facing accusations of ties to the late offender.
summary: Ads aired in the final stretch of the midterm campaign that accuse Republican candidates of protecting Jeffrey Epstein. The ads, released by Democratic candidates or supporting groups, claim Republicans voted against legislation to release Epstein-related files and aim to evoke an emotional response.
author: Guardian World

title: Fallon Sherrock defeats world darts No 1 Luke Littler on Netflix live TV
content:
Fallon Sherrock became the 15th amateur challenger to face world darts No. 1 Luke Littler in the Netflix‑streamed programme “Beat Luke Littler” on Friday evening, and she defeated him, securing the £501,000 prize awarded to any of the 20 amateurs who beat Littler in a single leg. Sherrock said she was “lost for words” after the victory.

The showdown formed part of Netflix’s first UK live entertainment event, airing on a night when audiences also could choose between the stream and the BBC final of “The Celebrity Traitors.”
summary: Fallon Sherrock, the 15th amateur challenger, beat world darts No 1 Luke Littler in the Netflix programme “Beat Luke Littler” on Friday evening. The win earned her a £501,000 prize, awarded to any amateur who defeats Littler in a single leg.
author: Guardian World

title: MoD documents say Cambridgeshire police breached US‑UK deal by handing US pilot case to military
content:
Ministry of Defence documents obtained by the Guardian reveal that officials privately accused Cambridgeshire police of breaching a US-UK agreement. The accusation stems from the police force’s decision to hand over the investigation of Captain Jacob Wulfson to US military authorities. Wulfson, an American fighter pilot, was accused of sexually assaulting Sarah Steele, a British woman, in his Cambridge flat. The incident involved the pilot strangling Steele.

The documents indicate that Cambridgeshire police allowed US military police to quickly assume control of the case. This transfer of jurisdiction led to the Ministry of Defence’s internal criticism, as officials believed the police force violated the terms of the bilateral deal by relinquishing the investigation to the US military.
summary: Ministry of Defence documents obtained by the Guardian say Cambridgeshire police handed the investigation of Capt Jacob Wulfson, an American fighter pilot accused of sexually assaulting and strangling Sarah Steele, to US military police. Officials say the handover breached a US‑UK agreement on jurisdiction.
author: Guardian World

title: Over 100 protest Palestine Action ban outside US embassy in London
content: Police start arresting demonstrators with Met commander alleging they are ‘essentially meeting to purposefully commit a crime’ Police have started making arrests at the first mass demonstration under Andy Burnham’s premiership opposing the proscription of Palestine Action. More than 100 people gathered outside the US embassy in Battersea, south London, holding signs that read: “I oppose genocide, I support Palestine Action.”
summary: Over 100 protest Palestine Action ban outside US embassy in London.
author: Guardian World

title: Oxfam charity shop profit falls 23% to £4.9m as UK secondhand market shifts
content:
UK charity shops are reporting a sharp decline in retail profits, a trend that some observers say could threaten the sector’s fundraising model. Oxfam, one of the country’s best‑known charity retailers, has described its trading environment as “exceptionally challenging” after its retail profit fell 23% year on year.

Unpublished accounts seen by the Financial Times show Oxfam’s retail profit dropped to £4.9 million in the most recent financial year, down from £6.4 million the year before. The decline is attributed in part to pressure from online secondhand clothing platforms, which have reshaped the market for charity shop sales.
summary: Oxfam charity shop profit falls 23% to £4.9m as UK secondhand market shifts.
author: Guardian World

title: John Healey budget rings‑fence preventative projects to protect long‑term savings
content:
John Healey’s budget contains a new rule that will ring‑fence “preventative” projects—spending that is expected to generate future savings that outweigh the initial cost. The rule was mentioned only briefly in Healey’s speech and occupies a single paragraph in the 166‑page budget document.  

Under the new rule, any spending classified as preventative will be protected from being diverted for more immediate needs. The policy is intended to keep such projects on track, ensuring that the anticipated long‑term savings are not eroded by short‑term budget pressures.  

Some commentators say the focus on long‑term outcomes could transform public spending and the way government decisions are made, though the rule’s practical effects remain to be seen.
summary: John Healey’s budget includes a decision to ring‑fence preventative projects whose future savings exceed their initial cost. The measure, mentioned briefly in his speech and a single paragraph of the 166‑page budget, aims to protect such spending from being used for immediate needs, representing a new focus on long‑term outcomes.
author: Guardian World

title: Starmer says UK must draw closer to Europe as US ties shift
content:
Keir Starmer, the former UK prime minister, stated in his first major political intervention since leaving No 10 that the UK and other European nations must draw closer together. He argued that Europe needs to unite as the United States becomes a less-reliable partner. Starmer warned that the shift in relations with Washington during Donald Trump’s presidency is unlikely to reset once the US president leaves the Oval Office.

In his remarks, the former leader cautioned European leaders about the threat posed by Russia and other actors. He accused them of being caught out by these new geopolitical realities twice already, emphasizing the need for a closer European alliance in response to the changing US relationship.
summary: Keir Starmer said the UK and other European nations must draw closer together as the US becomes a less‑reliable partner. He said the shift in relations with Washington during Donald Trump’s presidency is not likely to reset once Trump leaves the Oval Office.
author: Guardian World

title: Protests in Germany and France as French interior minister warns against Halloween masks
content: France’s interior minister Laurent Nuñez warned protesters that wearing Halloween masks could lead to fines. Demonstrations have begun in Paris, with participants marching from the Porte de Bagnolet, and similar rallies are occurring in Lille and Lyon. In Paris, crowds have gathered as two French student unions have announced plans to block schools and universities on Tuesday and Thursday. The minister’s warning and the coordinated protests are shaping the current unrest across several French cities.
summary: French interior minister Laurent Nuñez warned that covering faces with Halloween costumes could result in fines. Protesters marched in Paris from Porte de Bagnolet and also gathered in Lille and Lyon, while two French student unions called for a blockade of schools and universities on Tuesday and Thursday.
author: Guardian World

title: SpaceX launches 27 Starlink satellites from California on Halloween
content:
SpaceX celebrated Halloween with a launch from California on October 31, 2026. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base at 12:04 a.m. EDT (0404 GMT) and carried 27 Starlink internet satellites into low‑Earth orbit (LEO). The launch occurred early in the morning, with the rocket’s first stage returning to Earth as planned. It touched down on the SpaceX drone ship “Of Course I Still Love You” in the Pacific Ocean about 8.5 minutes after liftoff.

The Falcon 9 booster used for the flight is designated B1093, and this was its 18th flight. For context, the record for a SpaceX first‑stage flight is 37, set by booster B1067 in August of the same year. The upper stage performed its deployment mission successfully, releasing the 27 Starlink satellites approximately 62 minutes after launch. Those satellites are now joining more than 11,000 other spacecraft in the Starlink megaconstellation, the largest satellite network ever assembled.

This launch marked the 118th Falcon 9 flight of 2026, with over 70 % of the company’s missions that year devoted to expanding the Starlink network. SpaceX has also flown its Falcon Heavy and Starship rockets three times each this year. While Falcon Heavy remains an operational vehicle, Starship is still in the test‑flight phase, with another Starship launch scheduled for sometime in November.
summary: A Falcon 9 rocket from Vandenberg Space Force Base launched 27 Starlink satellites into low Earth orbit on Oct. 31, 2026. The booster, B1093, completed its 18th flight, landing its first stage on the drone ship "Of Course I Still Love You" and deploying the satellites 62 minutes after launch.
author: Space.com

title: Australia to Face Cook Islands in Rugby League World Cup Match
content:
The Australian men’s rugby league team, the Kangaroos, will face the Cook Islands in Townsville in a Rugby League World Cup match scheduled to kick off at 7:05pm local time. A victory for Australia would secure the top position in Pool A, allowing them to advance to the semi-finals. In that scenario, New Zealand would finish second in the group and also qualify for the semi-finals.

The tournament’s semi-final matchups depend on the outcome of the subsequent Tonga versus Samoa match. The winner of that game would top the group to face New Zealand, while the loser would finish second and play Australia. However, if Tonga wins by more than 46 points, England would progress as runners-up instead.

Ticket demand for the event has been exceptionally high, catching organizers off guard. A proposal to relocate the Sunday Tonga-Samoa match from CommBank to Accor Stadium at Olympic Park, which the NRL estimated could have attracted 60,000 fans, was rejected because it would have conflicted with pre-booked concerts.
summary: Australia to Face Cook Islands in Rugby League World Cup Match.
author: Guardian Sport

title: England miss Adil Rashid in tri‑series, aim to correct tactics in Australia
content:
England’s campaign in the KFC Presents Bank Alfalah ODI Tri-Series ended without a trophy, despite initial momentum. The team had previously defeated Sri Lanka both at home and away, and had secured a victory against Pakistan during the summer with the Dukes ball. However, in the final three games of the tri-series against Pakistan and Sri Lanka, England failed to convert strong positions into wins, a result described as puzzling due to the absence of leg-spinner Adil Rashid.

In a match against Sri Lanka, England posted a total of 429, relying on a strategy of scoring a large target to apply pressure. Despite batting efforts from Pavan Rathnayake and Dasun Shanaka, England could not secure the win. Captain Harry Brook became the first player to finish on the losing side after scoring an ODI double hundred. The article notes that while the tactical decision to exclude Rashid cost England the series, there is no need for immediate panic as the team can address these issues in upcoming matches in Australia.
summary: England miss Adil Rashid in tri‑series, aim to correct tactics in Australia.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Joanna Wietrzyk wins Hamburg Hyrox after Beijing incident
content:
Australian Hyrox athlete Joanna Wietrzyk claimed victory in the first event of the season in Hamburg, marking a return to the competition after a controversial incident in Beijing.  

Last month, Wietrzyk won a Hyrox event in Beijing but was seen soiling herself during the race. She apologized, forfeited the points, and faced a stinging backlash after footage of her continuing the demanding exercises with fecal matter running down her legs went viral on social media.  

She returned in style, winning the endurance sports event in Hamburg.
summary: Joanna Wietrzyk won the first event of the new Hyrox season in Hamburg. She previously won a Hyrox race in Beijing but forfeited the points after video showed her continuing the competition while soiled, leading to public backlash.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Stevens to appear alongside El-Sayed for first time in months, but expects apology
content: Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Mich.) will appear alongside Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed on Sunday for the first time in months. This event marks a reluctant show of unity following Stevens’ criticism of El-Sayed’s comments about Israel. Stevens confirmed her participation in a statement posted to X on Friday and expects an apology.
summary: Rep. Haley Stevens (D-Mich.) on Sunday will appear alongside Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed for the first time in months in what appears to be a reluctant show of unity after criticizing the Democratic nominee for his comments about Israel.
author: The Hill

title: Ro Khanna positions himself as progressive leader for 2028 Democratic primary
content: Rep. Ro Khanna is positioning himself as a leading figure for progressives ahead of the 2028 Democratic primary. He promotes his brand of progressive capitalism and seeks to build broad coalitions across the political spectrum.
summary: Rep. Ro Khanna is positioning himself as a leading figure for progressives ahead of the 2028 Democratic primary. He promotes progressive capitalism and seeks to build broad coalitions across the political spectrum.

title: GOP House member on ’embarrassing’ South Carolina prospects: ‘Darline is dragging Rs’
content: A House Republican described the competitive South Carolina Senate race as “embarrassing,” saying incumbent Sen. Darline Graham (R) is “dragging Rs down the ticket.” He noted Republicans originally won the seat by 18 points and added that the closeness now requires the speaker to travel to South Carolina to help the Republican candidate finish the race.

Darline Graham (R) is “dragging Rs down the ticket.” He noted Republicans won the seat by 18 points and that the speaker must come to South Carolina’s 1st district to pull the Republican across the finish line.

title: Federal Reserve keeps rates at 3.75%‑4% as inflation linked to energy costs
content: The Federal Reserve kept its benchmark interest rate unchanged, holding it in the 3.75 percent to 4 percent range at its most recent policy meeting. Analysts noted that the latest inflation surge appears to stem chiefly from higher energy costs rather than from broad‑based economic pressure.
summary: The Federal Reserve kept interest rates between 3.75 percent and 4 percent at its recent meeting. Analysis suggested that recent inflation was driven mainly by energy costs rather than broad economic pressure.
author: The Hill

title: Charlamagne criticizes Nicki Minaj for targeting Kathy Hochul but not Trump
content: Charlamagne criticized Nicki Minaj for condemning New York Governor Kathy Hochul while not applying the same criticism to former President Donald Trump. The commentary notes that Minaj is entitled to her political views, but argues that moral authority calls for consistent scrutiny of both opponents and those she supports.
summary: Charlamagne criticized Nicki Minaj for condemning Kathy Hochul while not condemning Trump. He said Minaj is entitled to her politics but should apply the same moral scrutiny to the people she supports.
author: The Hill

title: Obamacare premiums on Healthcare.gov to rise double digits in 2027
content: A report published Friday by health research group KFF indicates that Obamacare enrollees could face a 13 % increase in health insurance premiums in 2027, following a 26 % rise from 2025 to 2026. This marks the second consecutive year of double‑digit premium increases.
summary: A report by health research group KFF projects the average cost of Obamacare health insurance on Healthcare.gov will increase 13 percent in 2027. That would represent a double‑digit premium increase for a second year after a 26 percent rise from 2025 to 2026.
author: The Hill

title: Judge Trina Thompson blocks DOJ threat to California election officials over noncitizen voting
content: A California federal judge issued a temporary restraining order on Friday that bars the Department of Justice from threatening election officials with criminal prosecution over noncitizen‑voting claims. The order, signed by U.S. District Judge Trina Thompson, was issued in response to a lawsuit filed by unions representing California election workers.
summary: A California federal judge Friday ordered the Trump administration to stop threatening election officials with criminal prosecution in its ongoing efforts to crack down on noncitizen voting. U.
