title: Prime Minister Burnham open to slavery apology but rejects reparations
content: The prime minister says Britain must "face up to the past" for its role in the transatlantic slave trade but reparations are "not the right answer".
summary: Prime Minister Burnham open to slavery apology but rejects reparations.
author: BBC Politics

title: Study finds 1 in 4 Americans exaggerate symptoms to obtain antibiotics
content: A new study reports that more than one‑quarter of Americans have exaggerated or fabricated symptoms to obtain antibiotics from their doctors, whether for themselves or their children. The nationwide survey, which included nearly 1,000 respondents, identified common reasons for this behavior, such as feeling very ill or needing to return to work or school.
summary: A new study found that more than a quarter of Americans have exaggerated or fabricated symptoms to obtain antibiotics for themselves or their children. The nationwide survey of nearly 1,000 respondents identified motivations such as feeling very sick or needing to return to work or school.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Study: Hospitalized patients have lower death and readmission rates with female doctors
content: A new ICES study led by a University of Toronto researcher found that hospitalized patients treated by female physicians were less likely to die or be readmitted than those cared for by male physicians. The findings suggest that care by female physicians may be linked to better short‑ and long‑term outcomes for patients with common medical diagnoses.
summary: Study: Hospitalized patients have lower death and readmission rates with female doctors.
author: Medical Xpress

title: CDK1 activity linked to breast cancer resistance to targeted therapy
content: Researchers at the Garvan Institute of Medical Research have found that the activity of the protein CDK1 in breast cancers is linked to how the tumors respond to a common targeted therapy. The observation suggests the protein could help guide more personalized treatment decisions for patients.
summary: Researchers at the Garvan Institute of Medical Research found that the activity of the protein CDK1 in breast cancers is linked to how the tumors respond to a common targeted therapy. The insight may help guide more personalized treatment approaches for patients.
author: Medical Xpress

title: People with HIV lose more years of life to smoking than to HIV
content: People with HIV are now losing more years of life to smoking than to the virus itself. Approximately 1.2 million Americans live with HIV, and while smoking prevalence among U.S. adults has dropped below 10% for the first time, the rate among those with HIV remains up to four times higher. Although many individuals with HIV express a desire to quit, their quit‑rate is considerably lower than that of the general population.
summary: People with HIV now lose more years of life to smoking than to HIV itself. About 1.2 million Americans are living with HIV, and while smoking among U.
author: Medical Xpress

title: UT study finds personal life stories aid recovery for personality disorder patients
content: University of Texas research indicates that personal life stories can aid both treatment and personal recovery. The study emphasizes asking individuals about their identity, influences, and future outlook, noting that these questions may be especially significant for people with personality disorders. Clinical psychologist and psychotherapist Silvia Pol’s Ph.D. research finds that focusing on personal narratives can help guide treatment decisions and support recovery processes.
summary: UT research shows how personal life stories can support treatment and personal recovery. Who are you, what has shaped you, and how do you see your future?
author: Medical Xpress

title: European researchers launch ten‑marker personalized score to gauge disease risk and aging
content:
Approximately 60 % of people older than 65 now live with two or more chronic conditions, according to studies conducted in several countries. This high prevalence of multimorbidity has prompted a focus on reversing the trend and encouraging healthier aging.

In response, European researchers have developed a new personalized indicator that uses ten blood markers to flag disease risk and assess healthy aging. By analyzing, with high precision, the chemicals the body produces to function, the score provides a detailed snapshot of a patient’s metabolism and aims to guide interventions that promote long‑term health.
summary: Studies in various countries indicate that about 60% of people over age 65 have two or more chronic conditions. European researchers have created a new personalized indicator that uses ten blood markers to precisely analyze metabolic chemicals and provide a detailed snapshot of disease risk and healthy aging.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Transcription systems influence chromatin dynamics in distinct nuclear regions
content:
DNA in the cell nucleus is packaged into nucleosomes, which are further assembled into chromatin. Traditionally, chromatin is divided into transcriptionally active euchromatin and relatively inactive heterochromatin.  

Recent observations show that nucleosomes are not static; they continuously move within the nucleus. This dynamic motion is closely linked to the physical organization of the genome and its functional state.
summary: DNA is wrapped around histone proteins to form nucleosomes that organize into chromatin, which is divided into transcriptionally active euchromatin and relatively inactive heterochromatin. Nucleosomes continuously move within the nucleus, and this motion is closely related to the physical organization and function of the genome.
author: Phys.org

title: Study finds pay‑to‑quit bonuses increase employee effort
content: Researchers from the University of Waterloo, Wilfrid Laurier University, and McMaster University tested pay‑to‑quit programs. Their study confirmed that offering employees money to leave results in those who refuse to quit working harder. The research also uncovered an unexpected benefit that had not been anticipated.
summary: Researchers at the University of Waterloo, Wilfrid Laurier University and McMaster University tested pay‑to‑quit programs. Their results showed that employees who declined the quit money worked harder, confirming the programs work and revealing an unexpected benefit.
author: Phys.org

title: Microquasar Jets Linked to Gamma-ray Binary's Gas Trail Outside Milky Way
content: In 2016 astronomers identified a binary star system in the nearby galaxy that emits unusually strong gamma‑rays. New observations have revealed a trail of cool molecular gas that appears to trace jets from a microquasar, one of the few such objects known outside the Milky Way, suggesting the jets are the source of the gamma‑ray emission.
summary: In 2016, a binary star system emitting unusually strong gamma rays was discovered in our galactic neighborhood. Astronomers have found a trail of cool molecular gas that suggests jets from a microquasar—one of the few known outside the Milky Way—are responsible.
author: Phys.org

title: Crop diversification tested in Rio Grande do Sul improves resilience and yields
content: Researchers at the Center for Carbon Research in Tropical Agriculture (CCARBON) of the University of São Paulo tested a diversification approach in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil. The study found that varying crop rotations and maintaining continuous vegetation cover on the soil helped shield crops from droughts and floods while also raising overall productivity.
summary: Varying crop rotations and keeping soil continuously covered with vegetation help protect crops against droughts and floods while boosting productivity. The technique was tested in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, by researchers from the Center for Carbon Research in Tropical Agriculture (CCARBON) at the University of São Paulo.
author: Phys.org

title: UTe₂ shows two superconductivity flavors under extreme pressure
content: UTe₂ under extreme pressure displays two distinct “flavors” of superconductivity, according to recent research. Quantum researchers are searching for a topological superconductor—a material that would enable major advances in quantum computing by combining those two superconducting flavors.
summary: UTe₂ exhibits two distinct flavors of superconductivity when subjected to extreme pressure. Quantum researchers are searching for a topological superconductor that could enable major advances in quantum computing by combining such flavors.
author: Phys.org

title: Study maps human urogenital organ development, shows coordinated signaling

title: Scribd reports security incident exposing email and partial credit‑card data
content:
Scribd, Inc., the parent company of Scribd, Slideshare, Everand and Fable, disclosed a security incident in a notice sent on Monday, 26 October 2026. The notice, issued by the company’s notification partner Epiq, states that an unauthorized third party may have accessed certain user data stored in one of Scribd’s systems.

According to the notice, the compromised information includes the user’s email address, the last four digits of their credit‑card number, country, credit‑card issuer, credit‑card expiry date and payment history (excluding full card details). Scribd reports no evidence that the data has been misused, but it is informing affected users as a precaution.

The company urges users to remain vigilant for phishing attempts that may impersonate Scribd, Slideshare, Everand or Fable, emphasizing that it will never request usernames, passwords or other sensitive information via email or text. Recipients are advised not to click links in suspicious messages and to access Scribd services directly through official web addresses or by calling the dedicated help line at +1‑877‑361‑9887 during Monday‑Friday hours of 11:00 a.m. to 11:00 p.m. Central European Time.

Scribd says it has secured the affected system, terminated the unauthorized access, and notified law enforcement as well as relevant data‑protection authorities. The company is also working with an expert third‑party cybersecurity firm to strengthen access controls and monitoring, and it references guidance from the National Cyber Security Center on avoiding phishing scams.
summary: Scribd reports security incident exposing email and partial credit‑card data.

title: Mouria coffeehouse in Exarchia closes after 44 years as lease not renewed
content:
Mouria coffeehouse in Athens’ Exarchia neighborhood has closed after its lease could not be renewed. The historic café, long associated with left‑wing solidarity, resistance, and radicalism, has served as a gathering place for writers, artists, poets, politicians, doctors, lawyers, radicals and revolutionaries for as long as anyone can remember.  

For 44 years, proprietor Christos Vanas—formerly a waiter—has opened the café each morning at 7 a.m. before having his first coffee, welcoming the diverse community that has made Mouria a symbol of the area’s countercultural heritage. The café’s closure marks the end of an era in a neighborhood that is rapidly gentrifying.
summary: Mouria coffeehouse in the Exarchia neighbourhood of Athens could not renew its lease and is closing. The cafe, run by proprietor Christos Vanas for 44 years, has long been a gathering place for writers, artists, poets, politicians, doctors, lawyers, radicals and revolutionaries.

title: Star Trek actor Patrick Stewart dies at 86, colleagues post tributes
content: As we all begin to absorb the bitter news of Patrick Stewart's death at the age of 86, a flood of personal tributes are pouring in, reflecting this global treasure's wonderful life lived with a dignity and bravado that few mortals possess. We’re getting just a hint of what Patrick Stewart meant to those who worked with him or knew him throughout his stellar career. Whether on stage with the Royal Shakespeare Company, on TV as the dashing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in " Star Trek: The Next Generation," and in Hollywood spectacles like 1984's "Dune," four " Star Trek " feature films, and the many "X-Men" movies in which he portrayed Professor Charles Xavier, Stewart was always the consummate professional. His final screen performance arrives on Dec. 18 with "Avengers: Doomsday" where he’ll present his Charles Xavier character once more. "Before everything else, Patrick was defined by being born and bred in Yorkshire, the proud county in the north of England which he loved to the end," Ian McKellen wrote on Instagram of his "X-Men" co-star and friend. "You could hear it in his accented voice and in the stern honesty with which he told you what he thought and felt. Yorkshiremen have no truck with half-truths or avoidance of big issues. He wore his heart on his sleeve, which made him a man to rely on, to admire and, in my case, love." Patrick Stewart and Ian McKellan in 2000's "X-Men." (Image credit: 20th Century Studios) William Shatner, a fellow Enterprise captain, offered his profound sense of loss on Stewart's passing. The legends shared the screen in 1994's "Star Trek: Generations." "What a heartbreaking week it has been. Sir Patrick Stewart was a friend, a colleague, and a magnificent actor," Shatner posted on Facebook. "From the stage to the bridge of the Enterprise, he brought intelligence, grace, and a deep sense of humanity to everything he did. Captain Picard stood for the best of us, and so did the man who played him. I was filled with affection and admiration for him and his work. My heart goes out to Sunny and his family. He will be deeply missed." Patrick Stewart and William Shatner star in 1994's "Star Trek: Generations." (Image credit: Paramount) Akiva Goldsman, co-creator of Paramount+'s " Star Trek: Picard " and "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds," delivered a sorrowful message in the aftermath of Stewart's death "Patrick was not only a true lion of the profession, he was the rarest of alchemists, one who could literally turn the written word into flesh and blood," Goldsman wrote. "Patrick was kind, strong, fiercely intelligent, collaborative, vulnerable and wise. His Captain Jean-Luc Picard permanently expanded the universe of 'Star Trek' without measure. He will be deeply missed by this one fan and by so many more." Stewart's "Star Trek: The Next Generation" family shared their grief and offered up poignant words to try to describe what effect he had on their lives and profession. "There's no one on this planet that I have acted with or directed more often than my late great friend Patrick Stewart," revealed actor and director Jonathan Frakes, who co-starred for over 35 years with Stewart as Commander Will Riker, in a touching statement. "He will be with me forever. May he rest in Peace." Jonathan Frakes and Patrick Stewart share a laugh in "Star Trek: The Next Generation." (Image credit: Paramount) Finally, Marina Sirtis posted a teary-eyed video in which she explained how much of an impact Stewart had on her life during their time together on "The Next Generation" series and films, in which she portrayed Counselor Deanna Troi beside him. "Patrick, I loved you with all my heart," she said on Instagram. "I know you're up there now, reunited with all those that you've loved. But to say that you'll be missed down here is probably the understatement of the century. It was an honor to work with Patrick. It was more than an honor; it was the privilege of my life to work with him."
summary: Star Trek actor Patrick Stewart dies at 86, colleagues post tributes.

title: Sketch Stadium enables AI agents to play Pictionary via Wakeshift SDK
content:
Sketch Stadium is a new platform that allows artificial intelligence agents to play Pictionary. The project was initially developed as a proof-of-concept for delivering push notifications to AI agents but has been released as a standalone demonstration. Users can connect their own agents to the platform or simply observe ongoing games via a provided link.

In the game, agents subscribe to game events and take turns either drawing or guessing clues. The scoring system awards one point for easy clues, two for medium, and three for hard. The developer noted that the initial version allowed agents to draw lines ten at a time to mimic real Pictionary, but this method proved ineffective. The platform now permits agents to use a subset of SVG for drawing, which has improved performance even for lower-cost models.

To integrate an agent, users do not need to create an account; they only need to add the MCP and authorize it. The project serves as a technical demo for Wakeshift, a cross-harness SDK designed to provide push notifications for agents. This tool attaches to an MCP to allow consumers to subscribe to real-time events and uses specific methods per harness to wake dormant agents.

The developer explained that agents often initiate processes with indeterminate completion times, such as continuous integration or waiting for approvals. Currently, there is no consistent method to wake agents via webhook or push notification, forcing reliance on polling or bespoke integrations. The developer previously addressed this challenge with Clawvisor, where long-polling was the best-supported method for recognizing out-of-band approval actions. Wakeshift aims to solve this by providing a simple SDK that upgrades automatically as harnesses adopt MCP events.
summary: The platform allows agents to subscribe to game events and take turns drawing or guessing using a subset of SVG. The project serves as a tech demo for Wakeshift, an SDK designed to provide push notifications for AI agents.

title: Demo Shows FlashAttention Kernel Derived from ~25 Lines of SQL Using New SQL Extensions
content:
A developer has shared a demonstration on Hacker News that automatically deduces a FlashAttention kernel using approximately 25 lines of SQL. The SQL code expresses vanilla attention, a feat made possible by three portable SQL extensions currently under development. These extensions include xarray-sql, a library designed to represent petabyte-scale array datasets in the cloud as tables; ddx, a database extension that adds automatic differentiation in the style of JAX to standard SQL; and einfold, a modular query planner for fast tensor contractions.

The project is built on the thesis that separating logical layers in tensor programs from physical layers is both more correct and more scalable. The author suggests that the relational model and algebra offer fresh perspectives on accelerator programming, proposing to formalize the "Bitter Lesson" of machine learning using relational algebra. The post invites interest from those working at the intersection of database theory and ML systems, directing them to a Discord community for further engagement.
summary: An automatic demo derives a FlashAttention kernel from about 25 lines of SQL using three portable SQL extensions: xarray-sql, ddx, and einfold. The authors invite readers to join their Discord community to explore relational algebra for accelerator programming.

title: Rare meteorite from Mars gives us a view into its ancient crust
content:
A team of scientists led by Yang Liu of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory has identified a third genuinely ancient Martian meteorite, Teghaza 001. Discovered in the Sahara Desert in Mali in 2022, the rock formed at least 4.1 billion years ago. This discovery adds to the limited number of known ancient Martian samples, which previously included Allan Hills 84001 from Antarctica and a rock from northwest Africa known as Black Beauty. The finding provides a new perspective on Mars’ ancient crust, as most other Martian meteorites on Earth are significantly younger, dating to 2.4 billion years or less.

Liu noted that the rarity of old Martian rocks on Earth may be due to the physical conditions required for a rock to leave the planet. A large impact is necessary to launch material into space, but not all rocks can survive such an event. Weak or loose material may fail to cement into a solid rock capable of overcoming Mars’ gravity. Consequently, the impact process itself acts as a natural filter, preventing weaker rocks from reaching Earth.
summary: Crater counts tell us that most of the Martian surface is more than 3 billion years old, but pieces of Mars we have on Earth tell a different story. The three main classes of Martian meteorites—shergottites, nakhlites, and chassignites—are all 2.4 billion years old or younger.

title: New World Screwworm Infestation Spreads to Arizona, 74 Animal Cases Reported
content:

The New World Screwworm (NWS) infestation has now spread to a third state, Arizona, joining New Mexico and Texas as the only U.S. states plagued by the parasites. Since the flies re‑invaded the country in June, authorities have identified 74 animal cases.

The flies lay hundreds of eggs in wounds and moist orifices of animals. The resulting maggots, which resemble screws, bore and twist into living flesh, causing severe and sometimes fatal wounds. After feeding, the maggots drop to the ground to develop into adult flies.

The infestation is described as a genuine fright this Halloween, with the maggots festering along the southern border and continuing to threaten pets in the affected states.

title: On this day in space! Oct. 30, 1964: NASA's weird Lunar Landing Research Vehicle takes 1st test flight to help Apollo astronauts land on the moon
content: On October 30, 1964, NASA's Lunar Landing Research Vehicle, or LLRV, took to the skies for the first time. The LLRV was a bizarre, four-legged flying contraption commonly known as the "Flying Bedstead." NASA used it to simulate moon landings and liftoffs on Earth to prepare for Apollo 11, the first crewed lunar landing. The first person to give it a whirl was the X-15 pilot Joe Walker. During this test flight, he reached an altitude of about 10 feet, and he hovered there for about a minute. He did this two more times that same day. In all, he completed more than 30 test flights with the LLRV. These test flights took place at NASA's Dryden Flight Research Center in Edwards, California. That facility has since been renamed the Armstrong Flight Research Center after Neil Armstrong, who also piloted — and famously crashed — the "Flying Bedstead" before he went to the moon. The first Lunar Landing Research Vehicle is pictured during a test flight at NASA's Dryden Flight Research Center in California. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Over 60 years ago this LLRV test flight was a critical step toward landing humans on the moon for the first time, a historic moment that both served an important political purpose while also showcasing the result of monumental scientific and technical progress. While images from this test flight might look like the team are having a bit of fun out in the desert, and perhaps they were, it was also deadly serious. The astronauts who signed onto these crewed missions were doing something that had never been attempted. They were putting their lives on the line for this progress, and this testing was a major piece in reassuring them and NASA that lunar landing could be accomplished, and safely. Today, as we return humans to the moon with NASA's Artemis program, we see parallels between testing done over 60 years ago and testing today. Right now, SpaceX and Blue Origin are testing their lunar landers for crewed lunar landings in the near-future. While we have now been to the moon and have safely and successfully landed humans before, these tests remain critical for the safety and success of the missions. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube.
summary: On October 30, 1964, NASA's Lunar Landing Research Vehicle, or LLRV, took to the skies for the first time. The LLRV was a bizarre, four-legged flying contraption commonly known as the "Flying Bedstead." NASA used it to simulate moon landings and liftoffs on Earth to prepare for Apollo 11, the first crewed lunar landing.

title: A Few Good Men review – Aaron Sorkin’s legal drama makes unwelcome return to stage
content:
Aaron Sorkin’s 1989 courtroom drama, A Few Good Men, has returned to the Broadway stage at Lincoln Center’s Vivian Beaumont theater in New York City. The revival features a retooled version of the classic play, which centers on a cocky military attorney defending two young marines who followed an illegal order with fatal results. The production’s reception has been mixed, with critics noting that unconvincing performances and an ill-fitting big stage have made the current iteration feel like a missed opportunity.

The narrative explores the tension between critiquing a hallowed institution and imbuing it with dignity, a theme comparable to how Sorkin’s The West Wing portrayed the Oval Office. The story is set at the US military base at Guantánamo Bay, where a marine has died under troubling circumstances. Colonel Jessep, the hardliner in command, serves as the ultimate enemy to the protagonist, navy lawyer Daniel Kaffee.

The source suggests that audiences seeking crackling drama and sentimentality about the military would be better served by watching the 1992 film adaptation rather than purchasing tickets to the stage production. Directed by Rob Reiner, the movie is described as a clever, old-fashioned crowd pleaser that received an Oscar nomination. It starred Tom Cruise as Kaffee and Jack Nicholson as Jessep, with the film culminating in a classic trial scene featuring the memorable line, “You can’t handle the truth!”
summary: A Few Good Men review – Aaron Sorkin’s legal drama makes unwelcome return to stage.

title: Patrick Stewart, Star Trek and X-Men actor, dies at 86
content:
Patrick Stewart has died at the age of 86. The actor was widely recognized for bringing gravitas and complexity to the screen, particularly through his roles as Jean-Luc Picard in Star Trek and Charles Xavier in the X-Men franchise. His Shakespearean training and sonorous voice established him as a unique charismatic force in Hollywood.

Stewart was a member of the Royal Shakespeare Company’s 1970s stage generation and had previously held small screen roles, including an intimidating portrayal of Sejanus in I, Claudius opposite Derek Jacobi. He achieved significant pop culture stardom by securing the role of Captain Jean-Luc Picard, the leader of the Federation starship USS Enterprise, in Star Trek: The Next Generation. The series, which served as a reboot of the original Star Trek, ran from 1987 to 1994 and spawned four feature films and a subsequent series, Star Trek: Picard.

Colleagues such as William Shatner have paid tribute to Stewart, noting that he stood for the best of humanity. His career demonstrated the commercial potential of British classical training in American cinema and television, showcasing the technique and style of Shakespearean actors within the industry.
summary: Patrick Stewart has died at the age of 86, leaving behind a legacy that included iconic roles as Jean-Luc Picard and Charles Xavier. His Shakespearean training and distinctive voice established him as a charismatic force in Hollywood, bridging British classical theater with American pop culture.

summary: The Canadian sketch show SCTV influenced The Simpsons and launched the careers of actors including Eugene Levy, Catherine O’Hara, and John Candy. title: Study: Wildlife trade involves twice as many species as previously estimated
content:
A study published in Science Advances reveals that the number of plant and animal species involved in the global wildlife trade is more than twice as high as previously estimated. The research indicates that over 100,000 species are currently traded, encompassing illegal smuggling, ornamental sales, and industries including fisheries, timber, and fashion.

The authors warn that significant gaps exist in global assessments of wildlife trade, noting that past estimates have failed to account for recent developments. Specifically, the study highlights the rapid expansion of the online exotic pet trade, where sellers can easily offer to ship spider eggs internationally or facilitate the clandestine transport of reptiles on aircraft.

This significant increase compounds existing financial pressures on households that were already struggling before the conflict began.

Wolfe highlights research conducted by his organization, previously reported by The Guardian, which found that electricity shutoffs in ten states rose by 28% over the last two years. Millions of Americans have been falling behind on utility bills, forcing difficult choices between paying for energy, food, medicine, and rent. The current situation presents these households with another round of rising costs for gasoline, electricity, and home heating. In response, Wolfe calls on Congress to take action to ensure families can afford to heat their homes before the winter season starts.

title: Study finds host protein albumin fuels inflammation in vaginal yeast infections
content:
Up to three‑quarters of women will experience a genital yeast infection at least once, and recurrent cases can markedly affect quality of life. While symptoms such as itching, burning and pain stem from the yeast Candida albicans, they are driven largely by an excessive immune response.  

An international research team led by the Leibniz‑HKI has identified that the host protein albumin amplifies the inflammatory cascade and concurrently protects the fungal pathogen from immune attack. The study detailing this mechanism was published in Nature Communications.

title: Tech sell-off erases nearly $1tn from Nasdaq after weak earnings
content:
A sell-off in technology stocks, which began earlier this month and intensified following disappointing earnings reports from major tech firms, drove US markets down by hundreds of billions of dollars on Friday. The decline has reduced the value of the tech-heavy Nasdaq exchange by nearly $1 trillion in one week and erased approximately $2 trillion in a month. Investors are reportedly questioning whether the billions of dollars being invested in artificial intelligence can generate returns quickly enough.

The S&P 500, an index of the 500 most valuable US companies, fell by more than 1% on Friday, losing hundreds of billions in market value. Despite setting an all-time high during October, the index is on track to erase its gains for the month. The weakness in technology stocks dragged the Nasdaq composite down by more than 3%, further erasing hundreds of billions in value. Meanwhile, the Dow Jones Industrial Average experienced a smaller decline.
summary: Disappointing earnings from leading tech companies drove US markets down by hundreds of billions of dollars, wiping nearly $1tn from the Nasdaq in one week. The S&P 500 fell by more than 1% and the Nasdaq composite dropped over 3% as investors questioned returns on AI investments.
